name: Ireland
description:
The Emerald Isle combines Celtic heritage with modern tech hubs. Dublin is a major European tech center with a vibrant culture, while the countryside offers stunning natural beauty and a warm Irish welcome.

## Key Highlights
- Major European tech and startup hub
- Vibrant culture with warm and friendly locals
- Stunning natural beauty and Celtic heritage
longdescription: Ireland is an island nation off the coast of Western Europe, known for its Celtic heritage, literary traditions, and increasingly prominent tech industry. Dublin, the capital, has transformed into a major European tech hub, hosting European headquarters for Facebook, Google, Apple, and other tech giants. Irish culture emphasizes storytelling, music, literature, and community bonds. The Irish are known for warmth, humor, and hospitality. The countryside is stunningly beautiful, with dramatic cliffs, green landscapes, misty mountains, and coastal regions. Irish literature and music have influenced world culture profoundly. The economy has grown significantly, driven by tech companies, pharmaceuticals, and financial services. Dublin's startup ecosystem rivals other European capitals. Ireland is an English-speaking country, making it accessible to international workers. Healthcare is decent though sometimes challenging. The cost of living, particularly in Dublin, has risen significantly due to tech industry growth and strong economy. Irish tax policies are favorable for businesses, attracting corporate investment. The weather is typically cool, rainy, and grey. Public transportation in Dublin is adequate; outside the capital, a car is often necessary. Ireland offers competitive salaries in tech, a thriving cultural scene, natural beauty, and English-speaking environment. Challenges include high housing costs, weather, and Brexit effects on trade. Ireland combines tech opportunity, cultural richness, natural beauty, warm people, and English-language accessibility, making it attractive for tech professionals and those seeking Celtic heritage with modern innovation.

visas.name: For highly skilled (Ireland)
visas.description: For highly skilled workers in occupations experiencing critical skills shortages in Ireland.

visas.name: Ireland Student Visa (Stamp 2)
visas.description: Ireland's student visa (Stamp 2) allows non-EEA nationals enrolled in a full-time course on Ireland's Interim List of Eligible Programmes (ILEP) to live and study in Ireland.
benefits: Study at Irish universities and colleges
Part-time work permitted (20hrs/week term time, 40hrs holidays)

visas.name: Ireland Join Family Visa
visas.description: Ireland's join family visa allows non-EEA nationals to join a family member who is an Irish citizen or legal resident, subject to income, accommodation, and relationship requirements.

visas.name: Ireland Immigrant Investor Programme
visas.description: Ireland's Immigrant Investor Programme grants residence to non-EEA nationals who make a qualifying investment of at least �1 million in an approved Irish enterprise fund or business.
benefits: Right to live, work and study in Ireland
Path to Irish citizenship after 5 years

visas.name: Ireland General Employment Permit
visas.description: Ireland's General Employment Permit allows non-EEA nationals to work in Ireland in occupations experiencing labour shortages, requiring a job offer from an Irish employer paying above the salary threshold.
benefits: Live and work legally in Ireland

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Ancestry-based citizenship available for up to 2 generations of Irish-born ancestors. Registration available for foreign-born children of Irish citizens.

Naturalization.desc:
**Requirements:** 1 year continuous + 4 years total out of last 8 years residence, English/Irish language, good character, knowledge of Irish law.

**Processing:** Through Department of Justice, 4-6 months typically.

Spouse and Family.desc: Spouses of Irish citizens may apply with reduced residence requirements of 3 years continuous.

EU Citizens.desc: EU citizens enjoy freedom of movement with pathway to citizenship after 5 years residence.

tax_advice:
- Ireland has favorable 12.5% corporate tax rate (R&D tax credit added benefit)
- Personal income tax: 20% and 40% rates with credits
- VAT at 23% (reduced rates of 13.5%, 9%, and 0%)
- Extensive tax treaty network (70+ countries)
- Non-residents taxed on Ireland-source income only
- Capital gains: 33% tax rate with annual exemption of €1,270
- Double taxation relief available
- IP holding companies and R&D activities heavily incentivized
local_tips:
- English nearly universal; Irish accent takes time to understand
- Bureaucracy improving; PPS number (Personal Public Service) essential
- Healthcare: Private insurance recommended though public system available
- Cost of living high, especially Dublin; consider regional cities
- Tax rate low; double taxation treaties with many countries
- Visa sponsorship available for skilled workers; Critical Skills Employment Permit
- Weather rainy and cool; embrace pub culture for social integration
